{{Short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:William Duke. UCLA, 2019.jpg|thumb|William Duke. UCLA, 2019]]
'''William Drexel Duke''' (born 1958) is an American mathematician specializing in [[number theory]].
Duke studied at the [[University of New Mexico]] and then at [[New York University]] (''Courant Institute''), from which he received his Ph.D. in 1986 under the direction of [[Peter Sarnak]].  After a postdoctoral stint at the [[University of California, San Diego]] he joined the faculty of [[Rutgers University]], where he stayed until becoming a Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA).  He was Chair of the mathematics department at UCLA from 2015 to 2018.<ref>[https://math.ucla.edu/people/ladder/wdduke Faculty profile], Department of Mathematics, [[University of California, Los Angeles]]. Accessed May 15, 2016.</ref>

==Honors==
Duke gave an Invited Address at the 1998 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Duke ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897], [[International Mathematical Union]].  Accessed May 15, 2016.</ref><ref>[http://www.ams.org/notices/199805/people.pdf Invited speakers for ICM-98], [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], '''45''' (1998), no. 5, p. 621</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Duke, William|chapter=Bounds for arithmetic multiplicities|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=163–172|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011651000}}</ref>  Duke gave an AMS Invited Address at a 2001 Fall sectional meeting of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in Irvine, California.<ref>[http://www.ams.org/meetings/sectional/2075_invited.html AMS Sectional Meeting Invited Addresses], [[American Mathematical Society]]. Accessed May 15, 2016</ref> He was selected as a fellow of the American Mathematical Society in 2016 "for contributions to analytic number theory and the theory of automorphic forms".<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190516101122/http://ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows |date=2019-05-16 }}, [[American Mathematical Society]]. Accessed May 15, 2016.</ref>

Duke is an Editorial Board Member for the book series "Monographs in Number Theory" published by [[World Scientific]].<ref>[http://www.worldscientific.com/series/mnt Monographs in Number Theory], (series info), [[World Scientific]]. Accessed May 15, 2016</ref>

==Selected publications==

* Duke, W. (1988) [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF01393993 Hyperbolic distribution problems and half-integral weight Maass forms], [[Inventiones Mathematicae]], '''92''', 73–90.
* Duke, W., Schulze-Pillot, R. (1993) [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF01234411 Representation of integers by positive ternary quadratic forms and equidistribution of lattice points on ellipsoids], [[Duke Mathematical Journal]], '''71''', 143–179.
* Duke, W., [[John Friedlander|Friedlander, J.]], [[Henryk Iwaniec|Iwaniec, H.]] (1993) [http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PID=GDZPPN002110717 Bounds for automorphic L-functions], [[Inventiones Mathematicae]], '''112''', 1–8.
* Duke, W., Friedlander, J., Iwaniec, H. (1994) [http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PID=GDZPPN002111551 Bounds for automorphic L-functions II], [[Inventiones Mathematicae]], '''115''', 219–239.
* Duke, W., Friedlander, J., Iwaniec, H. (1995), [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2118527?seq=1#page_scan_tab_contents Equidistribution of roots of a quadratic congruence to prime moduli], [[Annals of Mathematics]], '''141''', 423–441.
* Duke, W. (1995) [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01245178 The critical order of vanishing of automorphic L-functions with large level], [[Inventiones Mathematicae]],  '''119''', 165–174.
* Duke, W., Kowalski, E. (2000), [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs002229900017 A problem of Linnik for elliptic curves and mean-value estimates for automorphic representations.  With an appendix by Dinakar Ramakrishnan], [[Inventiones Mathematicae]], '''139''', 1–39.
* Duke, W., Friedlander, J., Iwaniec, H. (2002), [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs002220200223 The subconvexity problem for Artin L-functions], [[Inventiones Mathematicae]],  '''149''', 489–577.
* W. Duke, [https://www.math.ucla.edu/~wdduke/preprints/bams4.pdf Continued fractions and modular functions], Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.) 42 (2005), 137--162 
* W. Duke, ¨O. Imamoglu,´A . Toth, [https://www.math.ucla.edu/~wdduke/preprints/annals-fin.pdf Cycle integrals of the j-function and mock modular forms], Ann. of Math. (2) 173 (2011), no. 2, 947-981. 
* W. Duke, ¨O. Imamoglu,´A . Toth,[https://www.math.ucla.edu/~wdduke/preprints/geometric.pdf Geometric invariants for real quadratic fields], Annals of Math. 184 (2016), no. 3, 949-990. 
* W. Duke,  [https://www.math.ucla.edu/~wdduke/preprints/elliptic.pdf On elliptic curves and binary quartic forms], IMRN (2022), no. 23, 19078–19104.
